title: Power Rankings: Competition tight for top-5 spot
heading: 2009-10 Power Rankings: Week 6
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Are these guys Artest-proof? They sure have been since Gasol came back, playing through Ron-Ron's appearance on "Jimmy Kimmel" in his shorts and then his Hennessy stories like almost no one saw or heard a thing.

rankings.summaryHtml: They've won seven in a row on the road. They've gone 8-1 since losing Jameer. They've won biggies at Boston and Atlanta and sit one disputed Miami basket away from an 11-game win streak. They've got to be No. 2.

rankings.summaryHtml: It's not this seven-game win streak that moved Boston up. Or a 9-1 road record that leads the league. It's how the Celts took it up a notch in back-to-back smotherings of San Antonio and OKC in their away green.

rankings.summaryHtml: Not easy at all to move up because of the way our top three are rolling, but the Cavs have also brought some normalcy to the upper reaches of the rankings thanks to that 12-0 record when they get to 100 points.

rankings.summaryHtml: The good news: Atlanta is a tidy 8-2 against teams at or above .500 after pulling out a W in Big D on Saturday. The bad news: Atlanta is just 6-4 against teams with losing records … and 3-4 overall since its 11-2 start.

rankings.summaryHtml: Does a win in San Antonio sufficiently atone for a streak-ending loss at home to the 1-15 Wolves? Especially when Melo cracks 30 points for the 12th time in his 20 games? We're actually inclined to say not quite.

rankings.summaryHtml: First real crisis for the Suns or an inevitable gas shortage after 15 of the first 21 games were roadies? Miffed as we are about that MSG showing right after we shot them up to No. 2, we're going with the latter.

rankings.summaryHtml: Just 82 points Friday night in a road L to Memphis. Just 75 points Saturday night in a home L to Atlanta. The Mavs can only hope losing two games in a row for the first time this season was just a very, very bad weekend.

rankings.summaryHtml: Lil' Aaron Brooks is generally seen as the offensive face of this scrappy incarnation of the Rockets. Just don't forget Carl Landry and his nine 20-point games ... after just four of those in his previous two seasons.

rankings.summaryHtml: This is the only team widely pegged for contention back in October that can't get near the top five. The other culprit besides injuries: San Antonio is 2-7 against teams over .500 after home L's to Boston and Denver.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Hornets are 5-5 under Jeff Bower because they somehow went 4-4 after CP3 hurt his ankle in Bower's opening game. We frankly expected none of that ... especially those home wins over Phoenix and Atlanta.

rankings.summaryHtml: Can't quibble with the 14-3 record posted by Alvin Gentry in November, so long as we don't forget Westy's 8-8 mark with the upstart Kings. Surely just as worthy of the first Western Conference coach of the month award.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Clips have won five of their past seven ... and no longer have a share of the NBA's worst start ever thanks to the Nets' plummet to 0-18. So life's not too bad, even if they have to wait until January for Blake Griffin.
